newsitem.title: USA: Jury out in Texas child murders case.
newsitem.headline: Jury out in Texas child murders case.

text.p: The jury broke off deliberations Friday and was to resume again Saturday after failing to reach a verdict in the case of a Texas mother accused of killing her two young sons in a fit of anger over financial problems and her weight.
Defence attorneys for Darlie Routier, charged with murder, said in closing arguments on Friday she was a doting mother who was falsely accused of the killings.
If found guilty by the jury of seven women and five men Routier, 27, could be sentenced to death by lethal injection. The jury deliberated for six hours Friday before stopping for the day.

Routier is accused of stabbing to death sons Devon, 6, and Damon, 5, while they slept June 6 in their Rowlett, Texas home near Dallas. She testified on Wednesday that an intruder killed the boys and attacked her before fleeing the house.
Final arguments were punctuated by a dramatic exchange between prosecutor Greg Davis and Routier.
"The last thing each of these children saw was their killer, their mother," Davis told the jury, staring at Routier in the hushed courtroom.
"You say liar now, but those two children saw this woman in a rage, coming down on them with a knife," Davis said.
Davis said Routier killed her sons because she was upset about the family's financial problems and dissatisfied with her appearance after gaining weight during her pregnancy with a third son, Drake.
"The money had run out, and she didn't like it," he said.

But defence attorney Doug Mulder said prosecutors had fabricated the money difficulties because they had no motive for the killings. He said husband Darin Routier's electronics firm brought in an income above $50,000 a year.
"That's a long way from skid row," Mulder said.
Prosecutor Toby Shook held the alleged murder weapon, a butcher knife, in front of the jury and spoke of how Damon was awakened by the attack.

"That's the most horrible aspect of this case, the part that will haunt all of us for the rest of our lives ... that Damon was awake, he opened his eyes and he saw his murderer, he saw his mother," he said.
Defence attorney Richard Mosty argued that the state's description of events was not logical and said the jury had heard no witness say that Routier had been a bad mother.
"It makes no sense that this woman could change from a doting mother to a psychotic killer," he said.
Davis attacked Routier's story about a "phantom intruder" and described it as "the Susan Smith defence," referring to the South Carolina woman convicted of drowning her two sons in 1994.
Smith claimed that a carjacker had killed the boys, but later confessed and is now in prison serving a life sentence.
Routier's trial was moved to Kerrville, about 60 miles (95 km) northwest of San Antonio, Texas, because of heavy pre-trial publicity.
